tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Open any URL in Firefox. Call when user says 'open github.com', 'go to localhost 3000', 'browse to anthropic.com', 'show me stackoverflow.com/questions/123'. Works with any domain, localhost with port numbers, or full URLs.

url.description: Full URL including protocol (e.g., 'https://github.com', 'http://localhost:3000') OR just domain (e.g., 'github.com', 'anthropic.com'). If user says 'localhost 3000' convert to 'http://localhost:3000'.

tools.name: run_shell_command
tools.description: Execute any shell command. Call when user explicitly says 'run command...', 'execute...', 'shell command...'. Use for git operations, npm commands, docker commands, system operations, or any CLI task. Do NOT use for opening URLs or window management (those have dedicated tools).

command.description: Full shell command to execute. Can include pipes, redirects, && chains, etc. Examples: 'npm install react', 'git commit -m "fix bug"', 'docker ps', 'cd ~/projects && npm run dev &'

tools.name: hyprland_dispatch
tools.description: Execute Hyprland window/workspace management commands. Call when user says 'workspace 3', 'focus firefox', 'fullscreen', 'move window to workspace 5', or any Hyprland-specific window management task.

params.description: Parameters for the action (e.g., '3' for workspace 3, '^(firefox)' for focusing firefox, 'address:0x...' for specific window). Can be empty string for actions that don't need params.

tools.name: ask_claude_code
tools.description: Invoke Claude Code CLI to work on the current project. Call when user says 'ask Claude to...', 'have Claude...', 'tell Claude Code...', 'Claude please...'. Use for coding tasks like refactoring, adding features, fixing bugs, writing tests, etc.

prompt.description: Task or question for Claude Code. Be specific and clear. Examples: 'refactor the groq module to use async/await', 'add tests for the clipboard module', 'fix the type errors in tools.rs', 'explain how the tool calling system works'

tools.name: ask_claude_code_in_directory
tools.description: Invoke Claude Code CLI in a specific project directory. Call when user says 'ask Claude to work on transcribe-rs', 'have Claude refactor the website project', or explicitly mentions a project name with a Claude task.

prompt.description: Task or question for Claude Code

tools.name: open_app_on_workspace
tools.description: Open an application on a specific Hyprland workspace. Call when user says 'open firefox on workspace 3', 'launch terminal on workspace 5', 'start code on workspace 2'.

notes.philosophy: Most operations on Linux are shell commands, so these tools provide semantic hints to the LLM about WHEN to use which pattern. The three core patterns are: (1) open URLs, (2) run shell commands, (3) manage windows. Everything else is just a variation.
notes.why_not_just_run_command: If you only had 'run_shell_command', the LLM would need to infer everything. By having 'open_url' and 'hyprland_dispatch' as separate tools, you give the LLM clear signals about common patterns. This reduces errors and makes intent clearer.

claude_code_integration.ad_hoc_mode: claude -p 'task description' runs Claude Code in ad hoc mode without a persistent chat
claude_code_integration.working_directory: You need to 'cd' to the project directory first, hence 'sh -c "cd /path && claude -p..."'
claude_code_integration.current_project: Update /home/seb/code/current-project to your active project, or use ask_claude_code_in_directory to specify
examples: Say: 'Ask Claude to add tests' → runs in current-project
Say: 'Ask Claude to refactor transcribe-rs' → extracts directory from context
Say: 'Have Claude explain the code' → works on current-project

advanced_patterns.combining_tools: You can still create specific tools that combine these patterns. For example, 'npm_install' could be a specialized wrapper around run_shell_command that adds better error handling or working directory context.
when_to_add_specific_tools: Complex multi-step process that should be atomic
Operations that need validation or safety checks
Commands where parameter extraction is tricky
advanced_patterns.generic_vs_specific: Start generic (6 tools). Add specific tools only when you notice yourself using the same pattern repeatedly.

url_handling.localhost_shorthand: When user says 'localhost 3000', LLM should convert to 'http://localhost:3000'
url_handling.domain_shorthand: When user says 'github.com', LLM should convert to 'https://github.com'
url_handling.full_urls: User can also provide full URLs like 'https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/fetch'

can_do_anything: cd ~/projects && npm run dev & → start dev server in background
git add -A && git commit -m 'fix' && git push → full git workflow
shell_command_power.use_cases: Anything not covered by open_url or hyprland_dispatch

directory_management.option_2: Use ask_claude_code_in_directory and let LLM extract project name
directory_management.option_3: Always cd in run_shell_command: 'cd ~/code/myproject && npm test'
